title: United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia
text: The United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia began on 26 September 2017, following the conclusion of the United Nations Mission in Colombia. The mission supports the peace process amid the Colombian conflict and was extended in 2023 by United Nations Security Council Resolution 2673.
wiki: United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia

title: Colombia assumes a two-year non-permanent seat at the United Nations Security Council.
text: The United Nations Security Council is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations, and is the United Nations' executive branch, having primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. Its powers, outlined in the UN Charter, include establishing peacekeeping operations, authorizing military action, and imposing international sanctions.

title: President Petro orders the mobilization of security forces along the Colombia–Venezuela border in response to the 2026 United States intervention in Venezuela.
text: On 3 January 2026, the United States launched a military strike in Venezuela and captured incumbent Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores. The US operation, codenamed Operation Absolute Resolve, began around 2 a.m.

title: The National Liberation Army (ELN) abducts five police officers from a bus in the Catatumbo region. They are released on 19 January.
text: The Camilista Union - National Liberation Army, also known as the National Liberation Army - Camilista Union (Ejército de Liberación Nacional - Unión Camilista, ELN-UC), and originally called the National Liberation Army (ELN), is a Colombian far-left guerrilla organization involved in the continuing Colombian conflict since 1964. The ELN advocates a composite Catholic communist ideology of Marxism–Leninism, Camil…

title: A Piper PA-31 Navajo crashes in Paipa, Boyacá Department, killing all six of its occupants, including singer Yeison Jiménez.
text: The Piper PA-31 Navajo is a family of twin-engined low-wing tricycle gear utility aircraft designed and built by Piper Aircraft for small cargo and feeder airlines, and as a corporate aircraft. Production ran from 1967 to 1984.

title: At least 27 people are killed in clashes between rival FARC dissident groups in El Retorno, Guaviare Department.
text: Guaviare is a department of Colombia. It is in the southern central region of the country.

title: Two freight wagons detach and roll into streets in Duitama, Boyacá Department, killing one person.
text: Boyacá is one of the thirty-two departments of Colombia, and the remnant of Boyacá State, one of the original nine states of the "United States of Colombia". Boyacá is centrally located within Colombia, almost entirely within the mountains of the Eastern Cordillera to the border with Venezuela, although the western end of the department extends to the Magdalena River at the town of Puerto Boyacá.

title: President Petro issues a decree reducing the wages of members of the Congress of Colombia by 30%, citing fiscal issues.
text: The Congress of the Republic of Colombia is the name given to Colombia's bicameral national legislature. The Congress of Colombia consists of the 103-seat Senate, and the 183-seat Chamber of Representatives, Members of both houses are elected by popular vote to serve four-year terms.

title: SATENA Flight 8849: a Beechcraft 1900 operated by SATENA, crashes near Ocaña, Norte de Santander, on its way from Cúcuta, killing all 15 people on board including congressman Diógenes Quintero.
text: On 28 January 2026, SATENA Flight 8849, a scheduled domestic flight in Colombia from Camilo Daza International Airport in Cúcuta to Aguas Claras Airport in Ocaña, crashed in Curasica, Playa de Belén, Norte de Santander. The Beechcraft 1900 operating the flight was carrying 13 passengers and two crew members.

title: The United Kingdom imposes sanctions on three Colombians accused of recruiting mercenaries for the Rapid Support Forces in the Sudanese civil war (2023–present).
text: The Rapid Support Forces are a Sudanese paramilitary force formerly operated by the Sudanese government. They originated as auxiliary force militias known as the Janjaweed used by the Sudanese government during the War in Darfur, which the government later restructured as a paramilitary organization in August 2013 under the command of Muhammad Dagalo, better known by his nom de guerre Hemedti.

title: Santiago Gallon Henao, a suspect in the 1994 killing of football player Andrés Escobar, is shot dead in Mexico.
text: Andrés Escobar Saldarriaga was a Colombian professional footballer who played as a centre-back. He played for Atlético Nacional, BSC Young Boys, and the Colombia national team.

title: Six people are killed in a methane explosion at the Mata Siete coal mine in Guachetá.
text: Methane is a chemical compound that has the chemical formula CH4 (one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms). It is a group-14 hydride, the simplest alkane, and the main constituent of natural gas.

title: 6–22 February – Colombia at the 2026 Winter Olympics
text: Colombia competed at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy, from 6 to 22 February 2026. It was the country's fourth appearance at the Winter Olympics, since its debut at the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver.

title: Two people are killed while four others are reported missing following an ambush on a convoy of senator Jairo Castellanos in Arauca Department.
text: Arauca is a department of Eastern Colombia located in the extreme north of the Orinoco Basin of Colombia (the Llanos Orientales), bordering Venezuela. The southern boundary of Arauca is formed by the Casanare and Meta Rivers, separating Arauca from the departments of Casanare and Vichada.

title: Senator Aida Quilcué and two bodyguards are briefly abducted from their vehicle in Cauca Department.
text: Aida Marina Quilcué Vivas is a Colombian politician and Indigenous civil leader who has served as a Senator of Colombia since 2022. A member of the Alternative Indigenous and Social Movement, she has served as a human rights advisor for UNESCO. In 1990, she was a health promoter for the Indigenous Association of Cauca.

title: The Search Unit for Disappeared Persons announces the discovery and identification of the remains of Catholic priest turned ELN leadzer Camilo Torres Restrepo, who was killed fighting the military in 1966.
text: Jorge Camilo Torres Restrepo, also known by his nom de guerre Argemiro, was a Colombian Catholic political leader, revolutionary, guerilla, priest, author and a leader of the National Liberation Army (ELN). During his life, he sought to reconcile revolutionary socialism and Catholicism, an ideology which became known as Camilism.

title: The ELN declares a unilateral ceasefire to allow for the holding of the 2026 Colombian parliamentary election on 8 March.
text: The 2026 Colombian legislative elections were held on Sunday, March 8. They elected the members of both chambers of the Congress of Colombia for the 2026–2030 term, from a total of 3,144 candidates.

title: Ángel Esteban Aguilar Morales aka Lobo Menor, an Ecuadorean national suspected of leading the Los Lobos gang, is arrested in Mexico and extradited to Colombia, where he is also wanted on charges of involvement with FARC dissidents.
text: Los Lobos is an Ecuadorian criminal and terrorist organization that specializes in drug trafficking and working as hitmen for international partners or allied groups. Los Lobos began as a splinter group of the Los Choneros drug cartel, but broke away in 2020 after the death of Jorge Luis Zambrano, along with Los Chone Killers and Los Tiguerones.

title: 2026 Colombian Air Force Lockheed C-130 crash: A Lockheed C-130 Hercules of the Colombian Aerospace Force crashes during takeoff from Caucayá Airport in Puerto Leguízamo en route to Tres de Mayo Airport in Puerto Asís, both in Putumayo…
text: On 23 March 2026, a Colombian Aerospace Force Lockheed C-130 Hercules crashed into dense jungle while taking off from Caucayá Airport in Puerto Leguízamo en route to Tres de Mayo Airport in Puerto Asís, both located in Colombia's Putumayo department near the border with Peru and Ecuador. There were 126 people on board, of whom 69 were killed, and 57 survived with injuries.
wiki: 2026 Colombian Air Force Lockheed C-130 crash

title: Three soldiers are killed in drone strikes carried out by the rebel group Comandos de la Frontera in Ipiales.
text: The Comandos de la Frontera, or Comandos de la Frontera-Ejército Bolivariano, is a criminal organisation classified as an Organised Armed Group (GAO) by the Colombian government, composed primarily of FARC dissidents, members of La Constru crime gang, and the far-right paramilitary United Self-Defence Forces of Colombia, as well as former military personnel. The organisation operates throughout the Putumayo Depart…

title: 2026 Cauca bombing: Twenty people are killed in a bomb attack on a bus blamed on FARC dissidents in Cauca Department.
text: On 25 April 2026, a bomb exploded along the Pan-American Highway in the municipality of Cajibío, department of Cauca, Colombia, setting fire to a bus and damaging several vehicles, which resulted in the killing of 20 civilians and the wounding of 36 more.

title: Three people are killed and at least 38 are injured when a monster truck crashes into spectators during a stunt performance at a public exhibition in Popayán.
text: On 3 May 2026, a monster truck lost control during a stunt performance at a public exhibition in Popayán, Cauca Department, Colombia, and drove into a crowd of spectators. The crash killed three people, including two minors, and injured at least 38 others.

title: At least seven people are killed in territorial clashes between the Misak and Nasa indigenous groups in Silvia, Cauca.
text: The Misak or Guambiano are an indigenous people of the department of Cauca in Colombia. Their language is known as Guambiano and is one of the Coconucan languages.

title: 2026 Colombian presidential election (first round): Right-wing candidate Abelardo de la Espriella wins a plurality of 43.7% of the vote, followed by left-wing candidate Iván Cepeda with 40.9%.
text: Presidential elections were held in Colombia on 31 May 2026. Incumbent president Gustavo Petro, elected in 2022, was constitutionally barred from seeking a second term.

title: 11 June–19 July – Colombia participates at the 2026 FIFA World Cup
text: The 2026 FIFA World Cup was the 23rd FIFA World Cup, the quadrennial international men's soccer championship contested by the national teams of the member associations of FIFA. The tournament began on June 11, 2026, and concluded on July 19 with Spain winning the championship for the second time. It was jointly hosted by 16 cities—11 in the United States, 3 in Mexico, and 2 in Canada.

title: Abelardo de la Espriella is inaugurated as president in a ceremony in Cali.
text: Abelardo Gabriel de la Espriella Otero is a Colombian lawyer, businessman, and politician who has served as the 36th president of Colombia since 2026. He is the founder and leader of the far-right Defenders of the Homeland party, established initially as a movement in 2024.

title: Two security guards are injured in a bomb attack on a tollbooth in Cauca Department.
text: Cauca Department is a department of Southwestern Colombia. Located in the southwestern part of the country, facing the Pacific Ocean to the west, the Valle del Cauca Department to the north, Tolima Department to the northeast, Huila Department to the east, and Nariño Department to the south.

title: A police officer is killed in a drone attack in Cesar Department.
text: Cesar Department, or simply Cesar, (Spanish pronunciation: ) is a department of Colombia located in the north of the country in the Caribbean region, bordering to the north with the Department of La Guajira, to the west with the Department of Magdalena and Department of Bolivar, to the south with Department of Santander, to the east with the Department of North Santander, and further to the east with the country o…

title: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake hits Chocó Department, killing 331 people.
text: On 10 August 2026, a Mw 7.4–7.5 earthquake struck the department of Chocó in Colombia, killing at least 335 people, injuring more than 4,600 others, leaving 111 confirmed missing and causing extensive damage across the country. The earthquake was felt across much of western and central Colombia and in parts of neighbouring Ecuador and Panama, and caused extensive damage in Cali, Pereira, Quibdó, Manizales, Armenia…

title: Colombia recognizes Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights.
text: The Golan Heights, or simply the Golan, is a basaltic plateau at the southwest corner of Syria, the majority of which has been occupied and administered by Israel since the 1967 Six-Day War. It is bordered by the Yarmouk River in the south, the Sea of Galilee and Hula Valley in the west, the Anti-Lebanon Mountains with Mount Hermon in the north and Wadi Raqqad in the east, with an alternative definition having it …

title: Congress elects Jorge Eliécer Laverde Vargas as Comptroller General.
text: The Office of the Comptroller General of the Republic of Colombia is a Colombian independent government institution that acts as the highest form of fiscal control in the country. As such, it has a mission to seek the proper allocation of resources and public funds and contribute to the modernization of the state, by means of continuous improvement in the various public entities.
wiki: Office of the Comptroller General of Colombia

title: An unlicensed gold mine collapses in Nariño Department, killing 13 workers and injuring seven others.
text: Nariño is a department of Colombia named after independence leader Antonio Nariño. Its capital is Pasto.

title: Viviane Morales resigns as education minister effective 7 September, citing personal reasons. She is replaced by Ilva Myriam Hoyos.
text: Viviane Aleyda Morales Hoyos is a Colombian politician who currently serves as the Minister of National Education since August 2026. She was the 6th Attorney General of Colombia and the first woman to hold that post.

title: Naín Andrés Pérez Toncel aka "Bendito Menor", a leader of the armed group Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada, is killed in a security operation in Riohacha.
text: The Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada are a Colombian criminal paramilitary organization operating in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta region.
wiki: Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada

title: Colombia–United States relations: The United States and Colombia sign a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation on critical minerals and rare earths during a visit by US secretary of state Marco Rubio to Barranquilla.
text: A memorandum of understanding is a type of agreement between two (bilateral) or more (multilateral) parties. It expresses a convergence of will between the parties, indicating an intended common line of action.

title: Colombia severs relations with Iran, alleging that the Iranian government has connections to "narco-terrorist groups that threaten the country's security."
text: Colombia seeks diplomatic and commercial relations with all countries, regardless of their ideologies or political or economic systems. For this reason, the Colombian economy is quite open, relying on international trade and following guidelines given by international law.

title: Colombia inaugurates its embassy in Jerusalem.
text: Colombia–Israel relations are the diplomatic relations between Colombia and Israel which were officially established on 1 July 1957. As of October 2026, Colombia is the second UN member state to recognize the Golan Heights as Israeli territory, and the tenth country to have its embassy in Jerusalem.

title: At the Hip Hop al parque festival, rapper Chelo Hop chants “Free Palestine” and “Out with what does not belong” and steps on the Israeli flag.
text: The flag of Israel was officially adopted on 28 October 1948. It is a white banner with three blue symbols: a pair of horizontal tallit-like stripes above and below a centred Star of David.
